feature_insights.num_subdomains: ⭐ STRONGEST SIGNAL (38.26%) - Phishing heavily exploits subdomain abuse and hierarchy confusion. Examples: bank.attacker.com, login.amazon-verify.attacker.com
feature_insights.num_slashes: 2nd strongest (22.51%) - Complex URL paths indicate obfuscation, phishing redirects, and hidden parameters
feature_insights.num_dots: 3rd strongest (17.80%) - Deeper subdomain hierarchy correlates with phishing attacks
feature_insights.url_length: 4th strongest (14.49%) - Benign URLs avg 20-40 chars, phishing URLs avg 50-100+ chars
feature_insights.num_hyphens: 5th (4.83%) - Less important than expected. Small dataset showed 32%, large dataset shows 4.8%. Typo domains less effective at scale
feature_insights.uses_https: 6th (1.35%) - Surprisingly low importance. Many phishing sites now use HTTPS to appear legitimate
feature_insights.has_suspicious_tld: 7th (0.45%) - Almost irrelevant on large dataset. Many legitimate domains use .tk/.ml
feature_insights.has_ip: 8th (0.32%) - Negligible impact. Many legitimate services use IP addresses

critical_discovery: Feature importance changes DRAMATICALLY with dataset scale. Small datasets (147 URLs) showed misleading patterns (hyphens=32%, TLD=28%). Large dataset (240K URLs) revealed truth: subdomains=38%, slashes=22%. This is crucial for production reliability.

scoring_formula.description: Hybrid approach combines proven heuristics (60%) with statistical ML signals (40%) for balanced detection and explainability

validation_notes: Model achieves 92.34% accuracy on balanced 240K URL dataset with 93.16% precision (low false alarms) and 91.39% recall (catches 91% of threats). ROC-AUC of 0.9778 indicates excellent discrimination between benign and malicious URLs.
